items.explanation: 71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation documented as an encounter diagnosis (8/22/2025) and carried in every cardiology clinic note since 10/10/2025. Current medications are levothyroxine only - no oral anticoagulant has ever been ordered in the chart. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1). The chart lists 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' as a past diagnosis but no active bleeding or documented decision to withhold anticoagulation; needs prescriber review.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list; 40 mg also exceeds the usual maximum in adults) is currently prescribed - last Cardiology Clinic order 7/15/2026, valid to 1/7/2027. Her most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 520 ms and Bazett QTc 562 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Prescriber review required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) has been prescribed since 3/1/2022 and is current (Cardiology Clinic order 6/17/2026, valid to 1/6/2027). Her most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows a regular sinus rhythm at 58/min with a markedly prolonged, late-peaking T wave: QT 588 ms, Bazett QTc 575 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026). She is 95 years old and also on warfarin; prescriber review of continued amiodarone is required.

Amiodarone (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 11/10/2025. Because the start predates 3/1/2026, the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met. (The tracing itself shows QTc 579 ms - see the separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was first ordered at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start is before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies with a 30-day window, i.e. an ECG was due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was recorded 3/8/2026 (24 days after the start), within the window. QTc on that tracing is 486 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 3/2/2026. The start is on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded 3/7/2026, 5 days after the start - requirement met. QTc 401 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026. Because the start is after 3/1/2026 the 14-day rule applies, so an ECG was due by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start - outside the required window - so the monitoring requirement was not met on time and remains outstanding as of the evaluation date.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026 (it was not on the medication list at the previous visit of 2/18/2026). Under the revised memo an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. Her only ECG (106035722) predates the start (12/25/2025), and no ECG has been obtained since. Overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was required within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. The telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, so whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside tracing arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026, which is after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date. No ECG has been done since the start (most recent tracing 104253928, 3/9/2025, QTc 477 ms), but the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr Kessler documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, within the window - requirement met.

80-year-old woman whose cardiology clinic notes from 9/12/2025 through 6/22/2026 all carry persistent atrial fibrillation in the problem list. Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only; no anticoagulant appears anywhere in her medication orders. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior TIA/cerebral infarction 2, vascular disease - old MI and coronary atherosclerosis 1, female 1). Aspirin is not an acceptable substitute for oral anticoagulation; needs prescriber review.

Anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 9/10/2026 by L. Nguyen, PharmD: home INR 3.4, warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol. A clinic pharmacist may adjust warfarin doses under the standing order, so this is a qualifying dose change and an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been drawn since the dose change. Overdue as of 9/24/2026.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation diagnosed during the 3/14/2025 admission for cerebral infarction due to embolism. Current medications (clinic note 6/23/2026) are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate - no anticoagulant is ordered. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior ischaemic stroke 2, female 1). Anticoagulation is strongly indicated for secondary stroke prevention; needs prescriber review.

48-year-old man with atrial fibrillation recorded at three admissions (2/26/2025, 6/17/2025, 6/23/2025) and listed as paroxysmal atrial fibrillation in every cardiology clinic note. The 6/2025 admissions also coded long-term (current) use of anticoagulants, but the current outpatient medication list (8/4/2026) is famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline - no anticoagulant order exists in the chart. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure 1, hypertension 1), which in a man meets the Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation. Needs prescriber review.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite this, apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/20/2026 (valid to 1/4/2027) and is listed as a current medication, alongside aspirin and clopidogrel. The anticoagulant is running again without the documented cardiology review of the bleeding event.

At the 7/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit the plan was to switch the anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban, but both drugs were ordered the same day and both remain active: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (7/15/2026, valid to 12/23/2026) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (7/15/2026, valid to 1/3/2027). The clinic note of 7/15/2026 lists both on the current medication list. Two concurrent oral anticoagulants (plus clopidogrel) is a duplicate-therapy bleeding hazard - the rivaroxaban order should have been stopped.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves and coarse fibrillatory activity, at ventricular rates of 139 and 144/min. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the patient is in atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is on the QT watch list and is currently prescribed (last Cardiology Clinic order 7/18/2026, valid to 12/26/2026). His most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 512 ms, Bazett QTc 546 ms, which is at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo of 1/15/2025. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are low-normal. Note the clinic note of 5/14/2024 recorded this same tracing as 'QT acceptable'. Prescriber review required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) has been continuously prescribed since 11/10/2025; the current Cardiology Clinic order is 7/12/2026, valid to 1/9/2027. His most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025, obtained as the post-start monitoring ECG) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT 570 ms and Bazett QTc 579 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal, so the prolongation is drug-related. Prescriber review required.

interpretations.explanation: Normal sinus rhythm at 83/min. Consistent P waves with PR about 145 ms, narrow QRS 76 ms, frontal axis +53 degrees, no conduction abnormality and QTc 420 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 101/min with normal PR 138 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms, axis +58 degrees and no conduction block. QTc 429 ms. This tracing was recorded 34 seconds after 102910502 and is effectively identical to it (sinus 100/min, QTc 427 ms) - no interval change.

Sinus rhythm at 97/min. A P wave precedes every QRS with a short PR of about 95 ms. QRS is narrow at 78 ms, axis +5 degrees, no bundle branch block. Bazett QTc is at the upper limit at about 491 ms (QT 386 ms at a rate of 97/min). Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a moderately rapid ventricular response, mean 97/min. The R-R intervals are irregularly irregular (0.38-1.10 s, coefficient of variation 0.30), there are no organised P waves, and a fibrillatory baseline is present, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS is narrow at 82 ms with no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -52 degrees (left axis deviation). QTc 437 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min with normal PR 136 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms, axis -4 degrees and no conduction block. QTc 360 ms. Compared with 108651109 a month earlier (sinus 66/min, QRS 108 ms, QTc 414 ms) the QRS is narrower and the QTc is 54 ms shorter - no categorical change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus bradycardia at 58/min: the R-R intervals are now regular with only gradual respiratory variation and low-amplitude atrial activity precedes each QRS (PR about 165 ms). QRS 90 ms, axis +38 degrees, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad, late T wave - QT 588 ms, Bazett QTc 575 ms. The prior tracing (100867733, three weeks earlier) showed atrial fibrillation at 131/min with coarse fibrillatory waves and QTc 461 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has increased by more than 110 ms on amiodarone. See the QT safety review item.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min with normal PR 134 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms, axis +45 degrees and no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is prolonged: QT 512 ms, Bazett QTc 546 ms. The prior tracing (100065910, 11/23/2022) had a QTc of 390 ms at a similar rate, so the QTc has increased by more than 150 ms. This is the tracing described in the 5/14/2024 note as 'QT acceptable' before escitalopram was started - see the QT safety review item.

Atrial flutter with 2:1 atrioventricular conduction. The ventricular response is regular at 141/min (R-R 0.40-0.45 s) and the baseline shows a continuous sawtooth with no isoelectric interval: a slow negative descent then abrupt upstroke in II, III and aVF with matching positive deflections in V1, repeating every ~210 ms (atrial rate about 285/min). No true PR interval can be measured. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +1 degree; QTc 426 ms. The prior tracing two days earlier (109839112) showed atrial fibrillation at 110/min, so the atrial fibrillation has organised into flutter.

Sinus tachycardia at 102/min with PR 128 ms, narrow QRS 90 ms, axis +46 degrees and no conduction block. QTc 461 ms. Compared with the tracing from the previous evening (101016166, sinus tachycardia 102/min, QTc 466 ms) there is no change.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean 144/min. The R-R intervals are irregularly irregular (0.35-0.65 s), there are no P waves, and coarse fibrillatory activity (about 70 microvolts) is present in II and V1, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 100 ms with no bundle branch block; axis -2 degrees; QTc 443 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (107914094, 17:13) showed the same rhythm at 139/min, so there is no interval change. Note the clinic note of 6/10/2026 describes these tracings as normal sinus rhythm at 72/min - see the rhythm documentation conflict item.

Sinus tachycardia at 120/min. A discrete P wave precedes each QRS (PR about 175 ms) and the rhythm is regular. QRS 96 ms, axis +54 degrees, no bundle branch block, QTc 414 ms. Compared with the 2016 tracing (106186980, sinus tachycardia 107/min, PR 170 ms, QTc 423 ms) there is no significant change.

Regular sinus rhythm with an upright, consistent P wave before every QRS. Narrow QRS, normal frontal axis, no bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the tracing two days earlier (105362569, sinus at 67/min, QTc 538 ms), the QTc has shortened by about 127 ms to 411 ms; rhythm and intervals are otherwise unchanged.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min with very little R-R variation and low-amplitude atrial activity about 135 ms before each QRS; interpreted as sinus rhythm. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis -25 degrees, QTc 441 ms. The prior tracing (104232242, 60/min, QTc 433 ms) had a markedly different frontal plane appearance with a negative lead I, most likely limb-lead misplacement on that recording; rhythm, conduction and QTc are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 69/min with PR 140 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms and QTc 415 ms; no bundle branch block or AV block. The frontal plane axis calculates to about -173 degrees (extreme axis deviation) because lead I and aVL are deeply negative while aVR is positive with preserved positive forces in V6 - a pattern that strongly suggests left/right arm lead reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation, and repeat tracing with correct lead placement is advised. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response, mean 53/min. The R-R intervals are irregularly irregular (0.70-1.17 s), no P waves are present and there is fibrillatory activity in V1, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +27 degrees. QTc 499 ms (rate-correction at this slow rate is unreliable). The tracing three days earlier (107873952) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with PR 154 ms and QTc 420 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation with a QTc increase of about 79 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min with PR 124 ms. QRS is 108 ms - slightly widened but below the 120 ms threshold, so no bundle branch block is diagnosed. Frontal axis +53 degrees. Repolarisation is abnormal with a biphasic T wave in the anterior leads; QT 456 ms, Bazett QTc 486 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.
Sinus rhythm at 74/min with PR 138 ms, QRS 92 ms, frontal axis +55 degrees and QTc 432 ms. No AV block and no bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular, with a P wave before each QRS (PR about 120 ms). QRS has narrowed to 94 ms so there is no longer a bundle branch block. The frontal axis is about +140 degrees (right axis deviation) with a predominantly negative lead I. QTc 438 ms. The tracing 13 hours earlier the same day (106516875) showed a wide-complex rhythm at 100/min with QRS 168 ms and a tall broad R in V1 (right bundle branch block pattern) and QTc 510 ms, so the bundle branch block has resolved and the QTc has fallen by about 72 ms.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean 153/min. R-R intervals are irregularly irregular (0.29-0.58 s) with no discernible P waves and fibrillatory activity in V1, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block, axis -18 degrees, QTc 428 ms. The tracing the previous evening (107374881) showed sinus rhythm at about 77/min with a single atrial premature beat, so this is new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 81/min with a clear upright P wave in lead II, PR 180 ms (upper normal), narrow QRS 82 ms, frontal axis +46 degrees and QTc 401 ms. No AV block or bundle branch block. This confirms the 3/7/2026 clinic note entry of 'ECG today: sinus rhythm'. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min with PR 154 ms and QRS 100 ms; no AV block or bundle branch block, frontal axis +37 degrees. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad low-amplitude T wave: QT 520 ms, Bazett QTc 562 ms. Compared with the 2020 tracing (107149156, sinus tachycardia 132/min, QTc 421 ms) the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms. The patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily - see the QT safety review item.

Sinus rhythm at 66/min with a clear P wave in lead II, PR about 155 ms, QRS 90 ms, frontal axis -19 degrees and QTc 402 ms. No AV block or bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min with a consistent P wave and normal PR. QRS is narrow with no conduction block; frontal axis -15 degrees (normal). QTc 448 ms. Compared with 102616671 (sinus 87/min, QTc 427 ms) there is no significant change in rhythm, conduction or repolarisation.

Sinus bradycardia at 58/min with PR 112 ms, narrow QRS 88 ms and frontal axis +62 degrees; no AV block or bundle branch block. The T wave is biphasic with deep anterior T inversion; QT 484 ms, Bazett QTc 477 ms - below the 500 ms review threshold. Compared with the tracing the previous morning (106045460, sinus 62/min, QTc 493 ms) there is no significant change.

Sinus rhythm at 82/min with PR 130 ms. QRS 106 ms - mildly widened but under 120 ms, so no bundle branch block is diagnosed. Frontal axis +34 degrees, QTc 452 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 107/min with a P wave before each QRS (PR about 155 ms), narrow QRS 72 ms, frontal axis +54 degrees and QTc 414 ms. No conduction abnormality. Compared with the 2019 tracing (107274479, sinus 75/min, PR 152 ms, QTc 438 ms) the rate is faster but rhythm, conduction and corrected QT are unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 61/min with a P wave before each QRS; PR about 195 ms, at the upper limit but not meeting criteria for first-degree AV block. The QRS is broad at 134 ms with a deep, wide QS/rS complex in V1 and a broad monophasic R in I, aVL and V6 - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis -21 degrees. QTc 472 ms (secondary repolarisation change from the conduction delay). The prior tracing (103686933) already showed left bundle branch block with QRS 132 ms and QTc 461 ms, so there is no interval change.
Sinus tachycardia at 109/min with PR 114 ms, narrow QRS 94 ms, frontal axis +35 degrees and QTc 448 ms. No AV block or bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 77/min with PR 152 ms, narrow QRS 74 ms, frontal axis +65 degrees and QTc 448 ms; no conduction abnormality. Compared with 109048192 (sinus 75/min, QTc 451 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.
Normal sinus rhythm at 72/min with PR 140 ms, QRS 88 ms, frontal axis +22 degrees and QTc 428 ms. No AV block or bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 61/min interrupted by one premature wide complex with a compensatory pause (ventricular premature beat), which accounts for the apparent R-R variability; the underlying sinus cycles are regular at about 0.98 s with a consistent P wave. PR measures about 200 ms, at the upper limit of normal but not meeting criteria for first-degree AV block. QRS 102 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis -32 degrees (left axis deviation); QTc 389 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 104/min with a discrete P wave before each QRS and a short-normal PR of 114 ms. QRS 100 ms, axis +39 degrees, no bundle branch block. QTc 439 ms by Bazett. The previous tracing (100698634) showed faster sinus tachycardia at 147/min; the rate has slowed but rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min - organised P waves with a constant PR of 138 ms have returned, and the R-R intervals are now regular. QRS 100 ms, axis +66 degrees, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is markedly abnormal with a broad, late-peaking T wave: QT 570 ms, Bazett QTc 579 ms. The prior tracing (108780865, 6/7/2025) showed an irregularly irregular rhythm without P waves at 47/min (atrial fibrillation with slow ventricular response) and QTc 435 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved - consistent with amiodarone started 11/10/2025 - at the cost of a QTc increase of about 144 ms. See the QT safety review item.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, regular, with a consistent P wave and PR 130 ms. QRS 98 ms, prominent S wave in V1 with normal precordial progression, axis +35 degrees, no conduction block. QTc 414 ms. Essentially unchanged from the prior tracing 102955795 (sinus tachycardia 115/min, QTc 409 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min. The R-R intervals are highly regular (1.14-1.18 s) and a low-amplitude but reproducible P wave precedes each QRS with PR about 170 ms, so despite this patient's history of atrial fibrillation the present rhythm is sinus. QRS 94 ms, axis +36 degrees, no bundle branch block, QTc 425 ms. Compared with 104629882 (sinus 58/min, QTc 421 ms) there is no significant change.

Sinus bradycardia at 54/min with a clear upright P wave in lead II. The PR interval measures about 215 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +3 degrees; QTc 405 ms. Compared with 103042067 (sinus bradycardia 51/min, PR at the upper limit, QTc 389 ms) there is no significant interval or rhythm change.

Sinus tachycardia at 120/min; each QRS is preceded by a consistent P wave with PR about 120 ms and the rhythm is regular. QRS 86 ms, axis +69 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QTc 414 ms (Bazett, rate-corrected from QT 292 ms). This is the only ECG for this patient, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a moderately rapid ventricular response, mean 97/min. Sinus bradycardia at 53/min with normal PR 136 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms, axis -4 degrees and no conduction block. QTc 360 ms. Compared with 108651109 a month earlier (sinus 66/min, QRS 108 ms, QTc 414 ms) the QRS is narrower and the QTc is 54 ms shorter - no categorical change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus bradycardia at 58/min: the R-R intervals are now regular with only gradual respiratory variation and low-amplitude atrial activity precedes each QRS (PR about 165 ms). The prior tracing (100867733, three weeks earlier) showed atrial fibrillation at 131/min with coarse fibrillatory waves and QTc 461 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has increased by more than 110 ms on amiodarone. See the QT safety review item.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min with normal PR 134 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms, axis +45 degrees and no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is prolonged: QT 512 ms, Bazett QTc 546 ms. This is the tracing described in the 5/14/2024 note as 'QT acceptable' before escitalopram was started - see the QT safety review item.

The prior tracing two days earlier (109839112) showed atrial fibrillation at 110/min, so the atrial fibrillation has organised into flutter.

Sinus tachycardia at 102/min with PR 128 ms, narrow QRS 90 ms, axis +46 degrees and no conduction block. QTc 461 ms. Compared with the tracing from the previous evening (101016166, sinus tachycardia 102/min, QTc 466 ms) there is no change.

Atrial fibrillation with a moderately rapid ventricular response, mean 97/min. Sinus bradycardia at 53/min with normal PR 136 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms, axis -4 degrees and no conduction block. QTc 360 ms. Compared with 108651109 a month earlier (sinus 66/min, QRS 108 ms, QTc 414 ms) the QRS is narrower and the QTc is 54 ms shorter - no categorical change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus bradycardia at 58/min: the R-R intervals are now regular with only gradual respiratory variation and low-amplitude atrial activity precedes each QRS (PR about 165 ms). QRS 90 ms, axis +38 degrees, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad, late T wave - QT 588 ms, Bazett QTc 575 ms. The prior tracing (100867733, three weeks earlier) showed atrial fibrillation at 131/min with coarse fibrillatory waves and QTc 461 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has increased by more than 110 ms on amiodarone. See the QT safety review item.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min with normal PR 134 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms, axis +45 degrees and no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is prolonged: QT 512 ms, Bazett QTc 546 ms. This is the tracing described in the 5/14/2024 note as 'QT acceptable' before escitalopram was started - see the QT safety review item.

Atrial flutter with 2:1 atrioventricular conduction. No true PR interval can be measured. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +1 degree; QTc 426 ms. The prior tracing two days earlier (109839112) showed atrial fibrillation at 110/min, so the atrial fibrillation has organised into flutter.

Sinus tachycardia at 102/min with PR 128 ms, narrow QRS 90 ms, axis +46 degrees and no conduction block. QTc 461 ms. Compared with the tracing from the previous evening (101016166, sinus tachycardia 102/min, QTc 466 ms) there is no change.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean 144/min. Regular sinus rhythm with an upright, consistent P wave before every QRS. Narrow QRS, normal frontal axis, no bundle branch block or AV block. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min with very little R-R variation and low-amplitude atrial activity about 135 ms before each QRS; interpreted as sinus rhythm. Sinus rhythm at 69/min with PR 140 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms and QTc 415 ms; no bundle branch block or AV block. The frontal plane axis calculates to about -173 degrees (extreme axis deviation) because lead I and aVL are deeply negative while aVR is positive with preserved positive forces in V6 - a pattern that strongly suggests left/right arm lead reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation, and repeat tracing with correct lead placement is advised. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response, mean 53/min. The tracing three days earlier (107873952) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with PR 154 ms and QTc 420 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation with a QTc increase of about 79 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min with PR 138 ms, QRS 92 ms, frontal axis +55 degrees and QTc 432 ms. No AV block and no bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

See the QT safety review item.

QRS 94 ms, axis +36 degrees, no bundle branch block, QTc 425 ms. Compared with 104629882 (sinus 58/min, QTc 421 ms) there is no significant change.

Sinus tachycardia at 120/min; each QRS is preceded by a consistent P wave with PR about 120 ms and the rhythm is regular. QRS 86 ms, axis +69 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Atrial fibrillation with a moderately rapid ventricular response, mean 97/min. Sinus bradycardia at 53/min with normal PR 136 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms, axis -4 degrees and no conduction block. QTc 360 ms. Compared with 108651109 a month earlier (sinus 66/min, QRS 108 ms, QTc 414 ms) the QRS is narrower and the QTc is 54 ms shorter - no categorical change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus bradycardia at 58/min: the R-R intervals are now regular with only gradual respiratory variation and low-amplitude atrial activity precedes each QRS (PR about 165 ms). QRS 90 ms, axis +38 degrees, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad, late T wave - QT 588 ms, Bazett QTc 575 ms. The prior tracing (100867733, three weeks earlier) showed atrial fibrillation at 131/min with coarse fibrillatory waves and QTc 461 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has increased by more than 110 ms on amiodarone. See the QT safety review item.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min with normal PR 134 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms, axis +45 degrees and no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is prolonged: QT 512 ms, Bazett QTc 546 ms. The prior tracing two days earlier (109839112) showed atrial fibrillation at 110/min, so the atrial fibrillation has organised into flutter.

Sinus tachycardia at 102/min with PR 128 ms, narrow QRS 90 ms, axis +46 degrees and no conduction block. QTc 461 ms. Compared with the tracing from the previous evening (101016166, sinus tachycardia 102/min, QTc 466 ms) there is no change.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean 144/min. Sinus rhythm at 74/min with PR 138 ms, QRS 92 ms, frontal axis +55 degrees and QTc 432 ms. No AV block and no bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1). The chart lists 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' as a past diagnosis but no active bleeding or documented decision to withhold anticoagulation; needs prescriber review.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list; 40 mg also exceeds the usual maximum in adults) is currently prescribed - last Cardiology Clinic order 7/15/2026, valid to 1/7/2027. Her most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 520 ms and Bazett QTc 562 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Prescriber review required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) has been prescribed since 3/1/2022 and is current (Cardiology Clinic order 6/17/2026, valid to 1/6/2027). Her most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows a regular sinus rhythm at 58/min with a markedly prolonged, late-peaking T wave: QT 588 ms, Bazett QTc 575 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026). She is 95 years old and also on warfarin; prescriber review of continued amiodarone is required.

Amiodarone (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 11/10/2025. Because the start predates 3/1/2026, the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met. (The tracing itself shows QTc 579 ms - see the separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was first ordered at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start is before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies with a 30-day window, i.e. an ECG was due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was recorded 3/8/2026 (24 days after the start), within the window. QTc on that tracing is 486 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 3/2/2026. The start is on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded 3/7/2026, 5 days after the start - requirement met. QTc 401 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026. Because the start is after 3/1/2026 the 14-day rule applies, so an ECG was due by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start - outside the required window - so the monitoring requirement was not met on time and remains outstanding as of the evaluation date.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026 (it was not on the medication list at the previous visit of 2/18/2026). Under the revised memo an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. Her only ECG (106035722) predates the start (12/25/2025), and no ECG has been obtained since. Overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was required within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. The telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, so whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside tracing arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026, which is after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date. No ECG has been done since the start (most recent tracing 104253928, 3/9/2025, QTc 477 ms), but the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr Kessler documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, within the window - requirement met.

80-year-old woman whose cardiology clinic notes from 9/12/2025 through 6/22/2026 all carry persistent atrial fibrillation in the problem list. Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only; no anticoagulant appears anywhere in her medication orders. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior TIA/cerebral infarction 2, vascular disease - old MI and coronary atherosclerosis 1, female 1). Aspirin is not an acceptable substitute for oral anticoagulation; needs prescriber review.

Anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 9/10/2026 by L. Nguyen, PharmD: home INR 3.4, warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol. A clinic pharmacist may adjust warfarin doses under the standing order, so this is a qualifying dose change and an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been drawn since the dose change. Overdue as of 9/24/2026.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation diagnosed during the 3/14/2025 admission for cerebral infarction due to embolism. Current medications (clinic note 6/23/2026) are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate - no anticoagulant is ordered. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior ischaemic stroke 2, female 1). Anticoagulation is strongly indicated for secondary stroke prevention; needs prescriber review.

48-year-old man with atrial fibrillation recorded at three admissions (2/26/2025, 6/17/2025, 6/23/2025) and listed as paroxysmal atrial fibrillation in every cardiology clinic note. The 6/2025 admissions also coded long-term (current) use of anticoagulants, but the current outpatient medication list (8/4/2026) is famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline - no anticoagulant order exists in the chart. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure 1, hypertension 1), which in a man meets the Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation. Needs prescriber review.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite this, apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/20/2026 (valid to 1/4/2027) and is listed as a current medication, alongside aspirin and clopidogrel. The anticoagulant is running again without the documented cardiology review of the bleeding event.

At the 7/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit the plan was to switch the anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban, but both drugs were ordered the same day and both remain active: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (7/15/2026, valid to 12/23/2026) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (7/15/2026, valid to 1/3/2027). The clinic note of 7/15/2026 lists both on the current medication list. Two concurrent oral anticoagulants (plus clopidogrel) is a duplicate-therapy bleeding hazard - the rivaroxaban order should have been stopped.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves and coarse fibrillatory activity, at ventricular rates of 139 and 144/min. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the patient is in atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is on the QT watch list and is currently prescribed (last Cardiology Clinic order 7/18/2026, valid to 12/26/2026). His most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 512 ms, Bazett QTc 546 ms, which is at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo of 1/15/2025. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are low-normal. Note the clinic note of 5/14/2024 recorded this same tracing as 'QT acceptable'. Prescriber review required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) has been continuously prescribed since 11/10/2025; the current Cardiology Clinic order is 7/12/2026, valid to 1/9/2027. His most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025, obtained as the post-start monitoring ECG) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT 570 ms and Bazett QTc 579 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal, so the prolongation is drug-related. Prescriber review required.

interpretations.explanation: Normal sinus rhythm at 83/min. Consistent P waves with PR about 145 ms, narrow QRS 76 ms, frontal axis +53 degrees, no conduction abnormality and QTc 420 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 101/min with normal PR 138 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms, axis +58 degrees and no conduction block. QTc 429 ms. This tracing was recorded 34 seconds after 102910502 and is effectively identical to it (sinus 100/min, QTc 427 ms) - no interval change.

Sinus rhythm at 97/min. A P wave precedes every QRS with a short PR of about 95 ms. QRS is narrow at 78 ms, axis +5 degrees, no bundle branch block. Bazett QTc is at the upper limit at about 491 ms (QT 386 ms at a rate of 97/min). Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a moderately rapid ventricular response, mean 97/min. The R-R intervals are irregularly irregular (0.38-1.10 s, coefficient of variation 0.30), there are no organised P waves, and a fibrillatory baseline is present, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS is narrow at 82 ms with no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -52 degrees (left axis deviation). QTc 437 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min with normal PR 136 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms, axis -4 degrees and no conduction block. QTc 360 ms. Compared with 108651109 a month earlier (sinus 66/min, QRS 108 ms, QTc 414 ms) the QRS is narrower and the QTc is 54 ms shorter - no categorical change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus bradycardia at 58/min: the R-R intervals are now regular with only gradual respiratory variation and low-amplitude atrial activity precedes each QRS (PR about 165 ms). QRS 90 ms, axis +38 degrees, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad, late T wave - QT 588 ms, Bazett QTc 575 ms. The prior tracing (100867733, three weeks earlier) showed atrial fibrillation at 131/min with coarse fibrillatory waves and QTc 461 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has increased by more than 110 ms on amiodarone. See the QT safety review item.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min with normal PR 134 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms, axis +45 degrees and no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is prolonged: QT 512 ms, Bazett QTc 546 ms. The prior tracing (100065910, 11/23/2022) had a QTc of 390 ms at a similar rate, so the QTc has increased by more than 150 ms. This is the tracing described in the 5/14/2024 note as 'QT acceptable' before escitalopram was started - see the QT safety review item.

Atrial flutter with 2:1 atrioventricular conduction. The ventricular response is regular at 141/min (R-R 0.40-0.45 s) and the baseline shows a continuous sawtooth with no isoelectric interval: a slow negative descent then abrupt upstroke in II, III and aVF with matching positive deflections in V1, repeating every ~210 ms (atrial rate about 285/min). No true PR interval can be measured. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +1 degree; QTc 426 ms. The prior tracing two days earlier (109839112) showed atrial fibrillation at 110/min, so the atrial fibrillation has organised into flutter.

Sinus tachycardia at 102/min with PR 128 ms, narrow QRS 90 ms, axis +46 degrees and no conduction block. QTc 461 ms. Compared with the tracing from the previous evening (101016166, sinus tachycardia 102/min, QTc 466 ms) there is no change.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean 144/min. The R-R intervals are irregularly irregular (0.35-0.65 s), there are no P waves, and coarse fibrillatory activity (about 70 microvolts) is present in II and V1, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 100 ms with no bundle branch block; axis -2 degrees; QTc 443 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (107914094, 17:13) showed the same rhythm at 139/min, so there is no interval change. Note the clinic note of 6/10/2026 describes these tracings as normal sinus rhythm at 72/min - see the rhythm documentation conflict item.

Sinus tachycardia at 120/min. A discrete P wave precedes each QRS (PR about 175 ms) and the rhythm is regular. QRS 96 ms, axis +54 degrees, no bundle branch block, QTc 414 ms. Compared with the 2016 tracing (106186980, sinus tachycardia 107/min, PR 170 ms, QTc 423 ms) there is no significant change.

Regular sinus rhythm with an upright, consistent P wave before every QRS. Narrow QRS, normal frontal axis, no bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the tracing two days earlier (105362569, sinus at 67/min, QTc 538 ms), the QTc has shortened by about 127 ms to 411 ms; rhythm and intervals are otherwise unchanged.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min with very little R-R variation and low-amplitude atrial activity about 135 ms before each QRS; interpreted as sinus rhythm. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis -25 degrees, QTc 441 ms. The prior tracing (104232242, 60/min, QTc 433 ms) had a markedly different frontal plane appearance with a negative lead I, most likely limb-lead misplacement on that recording; rhythm, conduction and QTc are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 69/min with PR 140 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms and QTc 415 ms; no bundle branch block or AV block. The frontal plane axis calculates to about -173 degrees (extreme axis deviation) because lead I and aVL are deeply negative while aVR is positive with preserved positive forces in V6 - a pattern that strongly suggests left/right arm lead reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation, and repeat tracing with correct lead placement is advised. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response, mean 53/min. The R-R intervals are irregularly irregular (0.70-1.17 s), no P waves are present and there is fibrillatory activity in V1, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +27 degrees. QTc 499 ms (rate-correction at this slow rate is unreliable). The tracing three days earlier (107873952) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with PR 154 ms and QTc 420 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation with a QTc increase of about 79 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min with PR 124 ms. QRS is 108 ms - slightly widened but below the 120 ms threshold, so no bundle branch block is diagnosed. Frontal axis +53 degrees. Repolarisation is abnormal with a biphasic T wave in the anterior leads; QT 456 ms, Bazett QTc 486 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.
Sinus rhythm at 74/min with PR 138 ms, QRS 92 ms, frontal axis +55 degrees and QTc 432 ms. No AV block and no bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular, with a P wave before each QRS (PR about 120 ms). QRS has narrowed to 94 ms so there is no longer a bundle branch block. The frontal axis is about +140 degrees (right axis deviation) with a predominantly negative lead I. QTc 438 ms. The tracing 13 hours earlier the same day (106516875) showed a wide-complex rhythm at 100/min with QRS 168 ms and a tall broad R in V1 (right bundle branch block pattern) and QTc 510 ms, so the bundle branch block has resolved and the QTc has fallen by about 72 ms.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean 153/min. R-R intervals are irregularly irregular (0.29-0.58 s) with no discernible P waves and fibrillatory activity in V1, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block, axis -18 degrees, QTc 428 ms. The tracing the previous evening (107374881) showed sinus rhythm at about 77/min with a single atrial premature beat, so this is new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 81/min with a clear upright P wave in lead II, PR 180 ms (upper normal), narrow QRS 82 ms, frontal axis +46 degrees and QTc 401 ms. No AV block or bundle branch block. This confirms the 3/7/2026 clinic note entry of 'ECG today: sinus rhythm'. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min with a consistent P wave and normal PR. QRS is narrow with no conduction block; frontal axis -15 degrees (normal). QTc 448 ms. Compared with 102616671 (sinus 87/min, QTc 427 ms) there is no significant change in rhythm, conduction or repolarisation.

Sinus tachycardia at 104/min with a discrete P wave before each QRS and a short-normal PR of 114 ms. QRS 100 ms, axis +39 degrees, no bundle branch block. QTc 439 ms by Bazett. The previous tracing (100698634) showed faster sinus tachycardia at 147/min; the rate has slowed but rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min - organised P waves with a constant PR of 138 ms have returned, and the R-R intervals are now regular. QRS 100 ms, axis +66 degrees, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is markedly abnormal with a broad, late-peaking T wave: QT 570 ms, Bazett QTc 579 ms. The prior tracing (108780865, 6/7/2025) showed an irregularly irregular rhythm without P waves at 47/min (atrial fibrillation with slow ventricular response) and QTc 435 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved - consistent with amiodarone started 11/10/2025 - at the cost of a QTc increase of about 144 ms. See the QT safety review item.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, regular, with a consistent P wave and PR 130 ms. QRS 98 ms, prominent S wave in V1 with normal precordial progression, axis +35 degrees, no conduction block. QTc 414 ms. Essentially unchanged from the prior tracing 102955795 (sinus tachycardia 115/min, QTc 409 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min. The R-R intervals are highly regular (1.14-1.18 s) and a low-amplitude but reproducible P wave precedes each QRS with PR about 170 ms, so despite this patient's history of atrial fibrillation the present rhythm is sinus. QRS 94 ms, axis +36 degrees, no bundle branch block, QTc 425 ms. Compared with 104629882 (sinus 58/min, QTc 421 ms) there is no significant change.

Sinus bradycardia at 54/min with a clear upright P wave in lead II. The PR interval measures about 215 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +3 degrees; QTc 405 ms. Compared with 103042067 (sinus bradycardia 51/min, PR at the upper limit, QTc 389 ms) there is no significant interval or rhythm change.

Sinus tachycardia at 120/min; each QRS is preceded by a consistent P wave with PR about 120 ms and the rhythm is regular. QRS 86 ms, axis +69 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QTc 414 ms (Bazett, rate-corrected from QT 292 ms). This is the only ECG for this patient, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 97/min. A P wave precedes every QRS with a short PR of about 95 ms. QRS is narrow at 78 ms, axis +5 degrees, no bundle branch block. Bazett QTc is at the upper limit at about 491 ms (QT 386 ms at a rate of 97/min). Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a moderately rapid ventricular response, mean 97/min. The R-R intervals are irregularly irregular (0.38-1.10 s, coefficient of variation 0.30), there are no organised P waves, and a fibrillatory baseline is present, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS is narrow at 82 ms with no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -52 degrees (left axis deviation). QTc 437 ms. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min with normal PR 136 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms, axis -4 degrees and no conduction block. QTc 360 ms. Compared with 108651109 a month earlier (sinus 66/min, QRS 108 ms, QTc 414 ms) the QRS is narrower and the QTc is 54 ms shorter - no categorical change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus bradycardia at 58/min: the R-R intervals are now regular with only gradual respiratory variation and low-amplitude atrial activity precedes each QRS (PR about 165 ms). QRS 90 ms, axis +38 degrees, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad, late T wave - QT 588 ms, Bazett QTc 575 ms. The prior tracing (100867733, three weeks earlier) showed atrial fibrillation at 131/min with coarse fibrillatory waves and QTc 461 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has increased by more than 110 ms on amiodarone. See the QT safety review item.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min with normal PR 134 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms, axis +45 degrees and no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is prolonged: QT 512 ms, Bazett QTc 546 ms. The prior tracing (100065910, 11/23/2022) had a QTc of 390 ms at a similar rate, so the QTc has increased by more than 150 ms. This is the tracing described in the 5/14/2024 note as 'QT acceptable' before escitalopram was started - see the QT safety review item.

Atrial flutter with 2:1 atrioventricular conduction. The ventricular response is regular at 141/min (R-R 0.40-0.45 s) and the baseline shows a continuous sawtooth with no isoelectric interval: a slow negative descent then abrupt upstroke in II, III and aVF with matching positive deflections in V1, repeating every ~210 ms (atrial rate about 285/min). No true PR interval can be measured. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +1 degree; QTc 426 ms. The prior tracing two days earlier (109839112) showed atrial fibrillation at 110/min, so the atrial fibrillation has organised into flutter.

Sinus tachycardia at 102/min with PR 128 ms, narrow QRS 90 ms, axis +46 degrees and no conduction block. QTc 461 ms. Compared with the tracing from the previous evening (101016166, sinus tachycardia 102/min, QTc 466 ms) there is no change.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean 144/min. The R-R intervals are irregularly irregular (0.35-0.65 s), there are no P waves, and coarse fibrillatory activity (about 70 microvolts) is present in II and V1, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 100 ms with no bundle branch block; axis -2 degrees; QTc 443 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (107914094, 17:13) showed the same rhythm at 139/min, so there is no interval change. Note the clinic note of 6/10/2026 describes these tracings as normal sinus rhythm at 72/min - see the rhythm documentation conflict item.

Sinus tachycardia at 120/min. A discrete P wave precedes each QRS (PR about 175 ms) and the rhythm is regular. QRS 96 ms, axis +54 degrees, no bundle branch block, QTc 414 ms. Compared with the 2016 tracing (106186980, sinus tachycardia 107/min, PR 170 ms, QTc 423 ms) there is no significant change.

Regular sinus rhythm with an upright, consistent P wave before every QRS. Narrow QRS, normal frontal axis, no bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the tracing two days earlier (105362569, sinus at 67/min, QTc 538 ms), the QTc has shortened by about 127 ms to 411 ms; rhythm and intervals are otherwise unchanged.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min with very little R-R variation and low-amplitude atrial activity about 135 ms before each QRS; interpreted as sinus rhythm. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis -25 degrees, QTc 441 ms. The prior tracing (104232242, 60/min, QTc 433 ms) had a markedly different frontal plane appearance with a negative lead I, most likely limb-lead misplacement on that recording; rhythm, conduction and QTc are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 69/min with PR 140 ms, narrow QRS 92 ms and QTc 415 ms; no bundle branch block or AV block. The frontal plane axis calculates to about -173 degrees (extreme axis deviation) because lead I and aVL are deeply negative while aVR is positive with preserved positive forces in V6 - a pattern that strongly suggests left/right arm lead reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation, and repeat tracing with correct lead placement is advised. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response, mean 53/min. The R-R intervals are irregularly irregular (0.70-1.17 s), no P waves are present and there is fibrillatory activity in V1, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block; axis +27 degrees. QTc 499 ms (rate-correction at this slow rate is unreliable). The tracing three days earlier (107873952) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with PR 154 ms and QTc 420 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation with a QTc increase of about 79 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min with PR 124 ms. QRS is 108 ms - slightly widened but below the 120 ms threshold, so no bundle branch block is diagnosed. Frontal axis +53 degrees. Repolarisation is abnormal with a biphasic T wave in the anterior leads; QT 456 ms, Bazett QTc 486 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.
Sinus rhythm at 74/min with PR 138 ms, QRS 92 ms, frontal axis +55 degrees and QTc 432 ms. No AV block and no bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular, with a P wave before each QRS (PR about 120 ms). QRS has narrowed to 94 ms so there is no longer a bundle branch block. The frontal axis is about +140 degrees (right axis deviation) with a predominantly negative lead I. QTc 438 ms. The tracing 13 hours earlier the same day (106516875) showed a wide-complex rhythm at 100/min with QRS 168 ms and a tall broad R in V1 (right bundle branch block pattern) and QTc 510 ms, so the bundle branch block has resolved and the QTc has fallen by about 72 ms.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, mean 153/min. R-R intervals are irregularly irregular (0.29-0.58 s) with no discernible P waves and fibrillatory activity in V1, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block, axis -18 degrees, QTc 428 ms. The tracing the previous evening (107374881) showed sinus rhythm at about 77/min with a single atrial premature beat, so this is new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 81/min with a clear upright P wave in lead II, PR 180 ms (upper normal), narrow QRS 82 ms, frontal axis +46 degrees and QTc 401 ms. No AV block or bundle branch block. This confirms the 3/7/2026 clinic note entry of 'ECG today: sinus rhythm'. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min with PR 154 ms and QRS 100 ms; no AV block or bundle branch block, frontal axis +37 degrees. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad low-amplitude T wave: QT 520 ms, Bazett QTc 562 ms. Compared with the 2020 tracing (107149156, sinus tachycardia 132/min, QTc 421 ms) the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms. The patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily - see the QT safety review item.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min with a consistent P wave and normal PR. QRS is narrow with no conduction block; frontal axis -15 degrees (normal). QTc 448 ms. Compared with 102616671 (sinus 87/min, QTc 427 ms) there is no significant change in rhythm, conduction or repolarisation.

Sinus tachycardia at 104/min with a discrete P wave before each QRS and a short-normal PR of 114 ms. QRS 100 ms, axis +39 degrees, no bundle branch block. QTc 439 ms by Bazett. The previous tracing (100698634) showed faster sinus tachycardia at 147/min; the rate has slowed but rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min - organised P waves with a constant PR of 138 ms have returned, and the R-R intervals are now regular. QRS 100 ms, axis +66 degrees, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is markedly abnormal with a broad, late-peaking T wave: QT 570 ms, Bazett QTc 579 ms. The prior tracing (108780865, 6/7/2025) showed an irregularly irregular rhythm without P waves at 47/min (atrial fibrillation with slow ventricular response) and QTc 435 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved - consistent with amiodarone started 11/10/2025 - at the cost of a QTc increase of about 144 ms. See the QT safety review item.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, regular, with a consistent P wave and PR 130 ms. QRS 98 ms, prominent S wave in V1 with normal precordial progression, axis +35 degrees, no conduction block. QTc 414 ms. Essentially unchanged from the prior tracing 102955795 (sinus tachycardia 115/min, QTc 409 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min. The R-R intervals are highly regular (1.14-1.18 s) and a low-amplitude but reproducible P wave precedes each QRS with PR about 170 ms, so despite this patient's history of atrial fibrillation the present rhythm is sinus. QRS 94 ms, axis +36 degrees, no bundle branch block, QTc 425 ms. Compared with 104629882 (sinus 58/min, QTc 421 ms) there is no significant change.

Sinus bradycardia at 54/min with a clear upright P wave in lead II. The PR interval measures about 215 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +3 degrees; QTc 405 ms. Compared with 103042067 (sinus bradycardia 51/min, PR at the upper limit, QTc 389 ms) there is no significant interval or rhythm change.

Sinus tachycardia at 120/min; each QRS is preceded by a consistent P wave with PR about 120 ms and the rhythm is regular. QRS 86 ms, axis +69 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QTc 414 ms (Bazett, rate-corrected from QT 292 ms). This is the only ECG for this patient, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

items.explanation: 71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation documented as an encounter diagnosis (8/22/2025) and carried in every cardiology clinic note since 10/10/2025. Current medications are levothyroxine only - no oral anticoagulant has ever been ordered in the chart. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1). The chart lists 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' as a past diagnosis but no active bleeding or documented decision to withhold anticoagulation; needs prescriber review.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list; 40 mg also exceeds the usual maximum in adults) is currently prescribed - last Cardiology Clinic order 7/15/2026, valid to 1/7/2027. Her most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 520 ms and Bazett QTc 562 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Prescriber review required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) has been prescribed since 3/1/2022 and is current (Cardiology Clinic order 6/17/2026, valid to 1/6/2027). Her most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows a regular sinus rhythm at 58/min with a markedly prolonged, late-peaking T wave: QT 588 ms, Bazett QTc 575 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026). She is 95 years old and also on warfarin; prescriber review of continued amiodarone is required.

Amiodarone (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 11/10/2025. Because the start predates 3/1/2026, the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met. (The tracing itself shows QTc 579 ms - see the separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was first ordered at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start is before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies with a 30-day window, i.e. an ECG was due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was recorded 3/8/2026 (24 days after the start), within the window. QTc on that tracing is 486 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 3/2/2026. The start is on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded 3/7/2026, 5 days after the start - requirement met. QTc 401 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026. Because the start is after 3/1/2026 the 14-day rule applies, so an ECG was due by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start - outside the required window - so the monitoring requirement was not met on time and remains outstanding as of the evaluation date.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026 (it was not on the medication list at the previous visit of 2/18/2026). Under the revised memo an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. Her only ECG (106035722) predates the start (12/25/2025), and no ECG has been obtained since. Overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was required within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. The telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, so whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside tracing arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026, which is after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date. No ECG has been done since the start (most recent tracing 104253928, 3/9/2025, QTc 477 ms), but the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr Kessler documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, within the window - requirement met.

80-year-old woman whose cardiology clinic notes from 9/12/2025 through 6/22/2026 all carry persistent atrial fibrillation in the problem list. Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only; no anticoagulant appears anywhere in her medication orders. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior TIA/cerebral infarction 2, vascular disease - old MI and coronary atherosclerosis 1, female 1). Aspirin is not an acceptable substitute for oral anticoagulation; needs prescriber review.

Anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 9/10/2026 by L. Nguyen, PharmD: home INR 3.4, warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol. A clinic pharmacist may adjust warfarin doses under the standing order, so this is a qualifying dose change and an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been drawn since the dose change. Overdue as of 9/24/2026.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation diagnosed during the 3/14/2025 admission for cerebral infarction due to embolism. Current medications (clinic note 6/23/2026) are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate - no anticoagulant is ordered. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior ischaemic stroke 2, female 1). Anticoagulation is strongly indicated for secondary stroke prevention; needs prescriber review.

48-year-old man with atrial fibrillation recorded at three admissions (2/26/2025, 6/17/2025, 6/23/2025) and listed as paroxysmal atrial fibrillation in every cardiology clinic note. The 6/2025 admissions also coded long-term (current) use of anticoagulants, but the current outpatient medication list (8/4/2026) is famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline - no anticoagulant order exists in the chart. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure 1, hypertension 1), which in a man meets the Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation. Needs prescriber review.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite this, apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/20/2026 (valid to 1/4/2027) and is listed as a current medication, alongside aspirin and clopidogrel. The anticoagulant is running again without the documented cardiology review of the bleeding event.

At the 7/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit the plan was to switch the anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban, but both drugs were ordered the same day and both remain active: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (7/15/2026, valid to 12/23/2026) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (7/15/2026, valid to 1/3/2027). The clinic note of 7/15/2026 lists both on the current medication list. Two concurrent oral anticoagulants (plus clopidogrel) is a duplicate-therapy bleeding hazard - the rivaroxaban order should have been stopped.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves and coarse fibrillatory activity, at ventricular rates of 139 and 144/min. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the patient is in atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is on the QT watch list and is currently prescribed (last Cardiology Clinic order 7/18/2026, valid to 12/26/2026). His most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 512 ms, Bazett QTc 546 ms, which is at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo of 1/15/2025. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are low-normal. Note the clinic note of 5/14/2024 recorded this same tracing as 'QT acceptable'. Prescriber review required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) has been continuously prescribed since 11/10/2025; the current Cardiology Clinic order is 7/12/2026, valid to 1/9/2027. His most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025, obtained as the post-start monitoring ECG) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT 570 ms and Bazett QTc 579 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal, so the prolongation is drug-related. Prescriber review required.

Aspirin is not an acceptable substitute for oral anticoagulation; needs prescriber review.

The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been drawn since the dose change. Overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Two concurrent oral anticoagulants (plus clopidogrel) is a duplicate-therapy bleeding hazard - the rivaroxaban order should have been stopped.
